Copilot appears directly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams — working on the file in front of you.

M365 Copilot (Premium)

With a Premium license, Copilot works inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Click the small Copilot button at the bottom-right of your document and the side pane opens — ready to draft, rewrite or analyze the file you have open.

Which one should I use? Start in the browser or the Copilot app for chatting, catching up and asking questions across your work — both are included with your sign-in. Use Copilot inside the Office apps when you want it to act on the document, spreadsheet, deck or email you're actively working on; this requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

Module 2

Copilot Fundamentals & Safe Use

Two things make Copilot safe and predictable at work: it's protected by the enterprise controls your organization already uses, and it grounds every answer in sources you choose. This module covers the fundamentals you'll lean on in every later lesson.

Reading / demo material — nothing to set up
Secure by design — Enterprise Data Protection (EDP)

Copilot doesn't bypass your security — it rides on top of it. Here's what's protecting you and where your data goes.

What Enterprise Data Protection gives you

On by default for anyone signed in with a work account.
  • Your data isn't used to train models. Your prompts, Copilot's responses, and the data it retrieves for grounding are never used to train the foundation models.
  • It inherits your existing protections. Copilot applies your organization's Microsoft 365 identity, security, compliance and privacy policies — including Microsoft Purview and sensitivity labels.
  • It respects permissions. Copilot can only surface content you already have access to — it never widens your reach.
  • Your data stays in the service boundary. Models are hosted in the Microsoft Cloud, within the Microsoft 365 service boundary; OpenAI has no access to your data or the model.

How a prompt flows

Every request is encrypted end-to-end.
1 · You prompt Copilot

From Chat or inside an app.

2 · Grounding via Microsoft Graph

Retrieves only content you're allowed to see, and/or the web.

3 · Responsible AI check

Prompt and results pass automated RAI checks.

4 · LLM in the Microsoft Cloud

Processed in the service boundary — not used for training.

5 · Compliance & Purview

Responses honor your data-protection policies.

6 · Response back to you

Returned with citations to its sources.

Nothing new to configure. Copilot automatically inherits the security, compliance and privacy controls your organization already set in Microsoft 365.

Terms you'll hear a lot

A few names sound alike. Here's how to tell them apart.

Chat Basic & Premium

The default Copilot chat experience — the prompt box you type into. It's the same chat surface whether you're on Copilot Chat (Basic) or M365 Copilot (Premium).

Edit in Copilot Premium

An in-app mode, previously called "Agent Mode," where Copilot takes a multi-step pass at your document, workbook or deck — working toward the outcome you described, step by step.

Word / Excel / PowerPoint Agents Basic & Premium

Task-focused agents built for a specific app, opened through M365 Copilot or Teams. Not the same as "Edit with Copilot."

Edit with Copilot in the open file

Assisted editing inside the file you have open — draft, rewrite or summarize what's in front of you (the ribbon button and side pane from Module 1).

Don't mix these up: Edit in Copilot (the multi-step mode, once called Agent Mode) is different from Edit with Copilot (assisted editing in your open file), which is different again from the Word / Excel / PowerPoint Agents (app-specific agents you open from Copilot or Teams).

More words you'll hear
Work IQ Premium

The intelligence layer that personalizes Copilot to you and your organization, grounding it in your work data.

Grounding

Giving Copilot trusted sources — the web, your files, or your work data through Work IQ — to base an answer on.

Agent

A customized version of Copilot scoped to specific instructions and knowledge for a task or role.

Agent Builder via M365 Copilot

The simple, no-code way to build your own agents directly inside Microsoft 365 Copilot (covered in Module 5).

Copilot Studio

The platform for building more sophisticated agents and workflows, with 1,400+ connectors to the apps your company uses.

Copilot Pages Basic & Premium

A persistent, shareable canvas for working on content together with Copilot and your team.

Notebooks Premium

A project-specific space where you group content so Copilot grounds its answers in just that material.

Create Basic & Premium

Copilot's AI design studio for generating branded images, video and graphics.

Researcher & Analyst Premium

Advanced reasoning agents — Researcher for deep, multi-step research; Analyst for data analysis.

Enterprise Data Protection (EDP) Basic & Premium

The security and privacy commitments that keep your prompts and data protected in Copilot (see the section above).

Web-grounded vs. Work IQ–grounded Chat

There aren't two separate chats anymore. There's one chat box with a single Work IQ toggle — flip it to control what Copilot grounds its answer in.

Work IQ onWork-grounded — your work data
Work IQ off

Web-grounded Chat

Copilot reasons over public web knowledge — ideal for research, drafting and general questions.

  • Open-web knowledge
  • Plus any files you attach
  • Available to Basic & Premium
Work IQ on

Work IQ–grounded Chat

Copilot also reasons over your work data across Microsoft 365 — emails, chats, meetings and files.

  • Everything web-grounded does
  • Your Microsoft Graph (permission-trimmed)
  • Full work grounding = Premium

Module 3

Prompting Like a Pro

A prompt is simply how you ask Copilot to do something — create, summarize, edit, transform or catch you up. Talk to it like a capable assistant: plain, clear language, with enough context to do the job well.

CreateSummarizeEditTransformCatch upLearn
The four prompt ingredients

The strongest prompts include four things — Goal, Context, Source and Expectations.

Goal
What do you want?

The response or outcome you need from Copilot.

Context
Why & for whom?

Why you need it and who is involved.

Source
From where?

Which files, people or samples Copilot should use.

Expectations
In what form?

How Copilot should respond — length, tone, format.

Generate 3–5 bullet points to prepare me for a meeting with Client X about their "Phase 3+" brand campaign. Focus on email and Teams chats since June. Use simple language so I can get up to speed quickly.
Goal Context Source Expectations
From vague to valuable

The same task — preparing for an AI Engineer interview — gets stronger as you add ingredients.

Good

"Help me prepare for an upcoming candidate interview for a new AI Engineer role in our IT department by creating a list of questions."

Better

"I'm an HR Manager preparing for a candidate interview for our new AI Engineer role in IT. Please prepare a list of appropriate questions so I look prepared during the interview."

Best

"I'm an HR Manager preparing for a candidate interview for our new AI Engineer role in IT. Please review the candidate's resume here: /[resume] and the position detail here: /[position doc] and give me a comprehensive list of questions to assess the candidate's fit for the position."

Extend the purpose

Before you hit send, think about what you'll actually do with the output — then ask Copilot to do the bigger job.

1 Why am I using this prompt?
2 What will I do with the output — send it on, reshape it?
3 Can I ask Copilot to take on the bigger task?
Just the task

"Recap the /[meeting] with a table of action items, owners and due dates."

The bigger job

"Write a follow-up email to the /[meeting] attendees with a table of decisions made, a table of actions and owners, and a list of topics for the next meeting."

Keep the conversation going

Copilot gets better as you follow up. Start broad, then refine — just like working with a colleague.

Generating ideas

Lead with a broad request, then add specifics.

Insightful meetings

Ask for a recap, then "what should I know?"

Storytelling

Ask for a draft, then guide it with details.

Deeper insights

Summarize a file, then ask follow-up questions.

Translation

Translate, then ask for tone or a regional dialect.

Technical problems

State the problem, then narrow it down step by step.

Seven prompting best practices
1

Length & clarity matter

Too short gives generic answers; too long and Copilot may miss instructions. Be clear and complete.

2

Break it into steps

Outline first, then expand each section, then add statistics and detail.

3

Use a persona

Tell Copilot the role to adopt for expert, tailored responses.

4

Ask what it needs

Not sure what to include? Ask Copilot what details it needs to succeed.

5

Think holistically

Look at whole processes — risk, comms, customer experience — not just single tasks.

6

Be curious

Experiment with different structures. Curiosity reveals new capabilities.

7

Test & refine

Iterate. Adjust prompts based on the results you get.

Hands-On Session — open Copilot and follow along

Run both prompts in Copilot in Word and compare the drafts.

Try it yourself — prompt face-off

STEP 1

Run the weak prompt

In Word, open Copilot and ask: "Write a job description for a senior program manager." Notice how generic it is.

STEP 2

Run the strong prompt

Now ask for a job description for a senior program manager focused on Azure cloud — concise, max two pages, with responsibilities and qualifications, using your standard specs.

STEP 3

Compare

Which draft is richer and more usable? Spot the Goal, Context, Source and Expectations you added.

Module 4

Copilot in the Office Apps

In Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, Copilot works right where you do. The key idea to grasp first: Copilot can write straight into the file you have open — not just answer in a side pane.

Editing Mode — Copilot writes into your open object

Inside an Office app, Copilot can do two things: chat with you in the side pane, or switch to Editing Mode and put content directly into the document, email, spreadsheet or deck in front of you.

Ask in chat

Copilot answers in the side pane. You read the result and copy what you need into your file.

Editing Mode

Copilot writes the content straight into the open object — drafting a Word document, filling Excel cells, building PowerPoint slides or composing an Outlook email.

Module 5

First-Party Agents

Beyond chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot ships with ready-made first-party agents — built by Microsoft and available right inside Copilot. No building required: open one and go.

What are first-party agents — and where to find them

First-party agents are specialized assistants built by Microsoft for specific jobs — research, data analysis, and more. You don't build them; you just open one and go. Find them all in the Agent Store: from the sidebar, choose Agents.

Word, Excel & PowerPoint Agents

These three agents are installed for you by Microsoft and live in the Copilot app — open one from the Tools menu or the All agents list in the sidebar. Tell it what you need in plain language and it creates a brand-new file for you, saved straight to your OneDrive. They're different from Edit with Copilot: rather than working inside a file you already have open, they build the document, workbook or deck from your prompt.

Copilot Chat (Basic)M365 Copilot (Premium)

Where they get their information. On Copilot Chat (Basic) the agents draw on the web and files you attach. With Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) they also ground in your work content through Work IQ — the files, emails, meetings and sites you already have permission to see.

Word Agent

Turn a prompt into a finished Word document — reports, proposals, policies, briefing notes or letters — structured with headings and ready to refine.

Draft from a brief

Describe the document and its audience; get a structured first draft you can polish in Word.

Reshape your material

Point it at meeting notes, a transcript or a data file and get a clean written report or summary.

Draft a two-page project proposal for a customer onboarding portal — goals, scope and timeline.
Write a one-page executive summary of /Q3 Business Review.docx.
Turn the notes from /Kickoff Meeting into a customer-ready FAQ.
Rewrite these bullet points as a formal project update memo.

PowerPoint Agent

Go from a prompt or a source document to a designed deck — the agent drafts the slides, organizes the flow and applies a clean layout.

Build a deck from a prompt

Give it the topic, audience and length; get a structured deck ready to present or tweak.

Document to slides

Point it at a Word report or notes and it builds a presentation that mirrors the key points.

Create a 10-slide overview introducing Microsoft 365 Copilot to new employees.
Build a customer pitch deck from /APAC Sales FY26.xlsx, ending with next steps.
Turn /Q3 Proposal.docx into a 6-slide customer presentation.
Add a closing slide that summarizes the key risks and mitigations.

Excel Agent

Create and work with a spreadsheet from a description — the agent builds the table, adds the formulas and can analyze data you give it.

Build a workbook

Describe the tracker or model you need; get a structured sheet with the right columns and formulas.

Analyze your data

Share a data file and ask for trends, a summary, a category breakdown or a chart.

Build a project budget tracker with columns for item, owner, planned cost, actual cost and variance.
Analyze /APAC Sales FY26.xlsx and summarize the top products by revenue.
Create a 12-month cash-flow model with monthly and annual totals.
Add a formula that flags any row where actual cost exceeds planned cost.

Every file these agents create is saved to your OneDrive, inside your organization's tenant — so it stays under the same security, sensitivity-label and compliance rules as the rest of your work.

M365 Copilot (Premium)
Researcher

Your built-in research assistant for the questions that need real digging — market scans, competitor analysis, or background for a big decision or meeting.

How it's designed. Researcher is built for depth over speed. It reasons through a question in several steps, drawing on both the web and your work content — files, emails, meetings and chats you have access to — and returns a comprehensive, source-cited report. It deliberately takes longer than a standard chat answer because it's doing thoughtful, multi-step analysis rather than a quick reply.

Market & competitor scans

Pull together a landscape on a market, competitor or trend — cited, so you can verify every claim.

Decision & meeting prep

Combine your internal documents with the web into a briefing before a big decision or customer meeting.

Research the managed-services market in Southeast Asia and summarize the top five players, with sources.
Prepare a briefing on /[customer] ahead of our renewal meeting, using my emails and the web.
Compare the leading cloud backup vendors on price, security and integrations.
What are the emerging risks in our industry this quarter? Cite your sources.
M365 Copilot (Premium)
Analyst

A virtual data analyst that turns raw, messy data into clear answers, tables and charts.

How it's designed. Analyst works like a data scientist on your team. It reasons through a dataset step by step — and can run Python code when a question calls for it — to surface trends, comparisons and anomalies, then explains its thinking and shows the visuals. It's built for the analytical questions that go beyond a quick formula in Excel.

Find the story in the data

Spot trends, seasonality and outliers across a spreadsheet or export — with charts to back them up.

Answer the hard questions

Run multi-step analysis — segments, correlations, forecasts — that a single formula can't handle.

Analyze /APAC Sales FY26.xlsx and show the revenue trend by quarter with a chart.
Find any anomalies or outliers in this expense data and explain them.
Segment these customers by spend and tell me what each group has in common.
Forecast next quarter's pipeline from the last eight quarters of data.
M365 Copilot (Premium)
Cowork

Cowork is about getting work done, not just answered — you delegate an outcome and Copilot carries out the steps. Find it on the Cowork tab in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

How it's designed. Cowork is built to take action, not just chat. You describe the outcome you want and it grounds the work in your emails, meetings, messages, files and data — powered by Work IQ — then works through the task across your Microsoft 365 apps. Think of it as delegating a multi-step job rather than asking a single question.

Delegate a multi-step task

Hand off a job that spans several apps and steps, and let Cowork work through it on your behalf.

Grounded in your work

Because it draws on your Outlook, Teams and files, the result reflects your real context — not a generic answer.

Pull together everything on /[project] from my email and Teams and draft a status summary.
Review last week's meetings and turn the action items into a tracked to-do list.
Draft replies to the follow-ups waiting in my inbox about the Q3 launch.
Compile the figures from /APAC Sales FY26.xlsx into a short update for my manager.

Configuring your Agent in Agent Builder

On the Configure tab you shape the agent through four parts.

1

Instructions

Tell the agent how to behave — its tasks, tone, rules, steps and examples. This is where your prompt becomes the agent’s standing brief. (Up to 8,000 characters.)

2

Knowledge

Choose the sources the agent grounds its answers in. Premium can use files, emails, chats, meetings, websites and the org chart; Basic is limited to specific websites.

3

Capabilities

Turn on what the agent can produce — create documents, charts and code, and create images.

4

Suggested prompts

Add starter prompts (a Title and a Message) so people know how to begin with your agent.

Character limits. Name — up to 30 characters. Description — up to 1,000. Instructions — up to 8,000. Keep instructions focused; for longer or more complex logic, split it into steps or move to Copilot Studio. Learn more →

Considerations: Grounded Knowledge vs. Attached Cloud Files

When you hand Copilot documents to work from, there are two ways to do it — and they behave differently. A knowledge source (for example, a SharePoint folder you add) lets Copilot find the relevant bits across many documents. Attaching a cloud file points Copilot straight at specific files so it reads them thoroughly. In short: knowledge sources optimize for relevance; attached files optimize for completeness.

Use a knowledge source when…
  • You're searching a large document library
  • You're answering FAQ-style questions
  • You're discovering things — "which policy mentions X?", "what are the common themes?"
Attach cloud files when…
  • Legal or policy review and validation
  • Exception analysis
  • "Make sure you don't miss anything" tasks on specific files
What to considerKnowledge source (SharePoint folder)Attached cloud file
How it finds answersSearches and pulls the most relevant pieces (semantic search)Reads the file you point it at, directly
Default behaviour"Find what's relevant""This file is the source"
Reads the whole file? Not necessarily — it picks relevant parts Practically yes (in chunks)
Risk of missing content Higher if your prompt is vague Low
How specific your prompt must beHighMedium
Best forQ&A across a large libraryDeep analysis of one to a few files

Rule of thumb. Reach for a knowledge source when you're searching a big pile of documents for the right answer. Attach the file(s) when you need Copilot to read specific documents from top to bottom — like a legal or policy review where missing a line matters.

Appendix · Optional

Beyond the Basics — Advanced & Optional Features

A grab-bag of deeper capabilities you'll come across as you explore Copilot. Handy to know, but not essential for everyday work — and a few get technical. We'll keep adding to this section over time.

Which tool should I use?

Copilot gives you a few different ways to work with a document — and the right one depends on what you're trying to do. Before you start, ask: how am I going to use this file? Your answer points to the right tool. (The same thinking works for both Word .docx and Excel .xlsx.)

1
Make specific changes to the file itself
→ Edit with Copilot (or Edit in Copilot / Agent Mode), right in the app
docx: fill a template, draft or rewrite a documentxlsx: build or edit the workbook, add formulas & charts
2
Get high-level analysis across several reports or datasets
→ The Analyst agent
docx: pull insights from multiple reportsxlsx: find trends across multiple datasets
3
Use the document(s) as a source to answer questions
→ Attach as a cloud file, or add as a Knowledge source
docx: one policy doc (attach) vs a SharePoint policy library (knowledge source)xlsx: one workbook (attach) vs a folder of data files (knowledge source) — xlsx suitability as grounding knowledge depends on the use case
4
Create a brand-new file from a conversation
→ The Word / Excel agent in M365 Copilot
docx: turn a discussion into a new documentxlsx: generate a new workbook from your ask

Scenario 3 is where Grounded Knowledge vs. Attached Cloud Files (Module 6) comes in — attach a file to read it closely, or use a knowledge source to search a whole library. If a task like this repeats, consider building an agent for it.
